common_name: Louise Photinia (Variegated Cream-Edged Red Tip Photinia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter through fall in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Louise's naturally tidy, upright habit needs less frequent shearing than plain Red Tip to stay dense.

directions: Louise is a British-bred Photinia x fraseri selection distinguished by irregular cream-to-pink margins that develop on the mature leaves, adding cool variegated color once the season's bronze-red new-growth flush has hardened off and turned green. Its more compact, naturally bushy, upright habit stays tidier between prunings than plain Red Tip or the larger-leaved Robusta, making it a good fit for a mid-size decorative hedge or specimen. Like other Photinia x fraseri selections it is vulnerable to Entomosporium leaf spot in humid, crowded plantings, so give it full sun to light shade, good air circulation, and well-drained soil. A light prune after the main spring growth flush keeps the plant dense and encourages fresh colorful new leaves.

common_name: Winecraft Black Smokebush (Compact Near-Black Foliage Smoke Tree)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Winecraft Black's compact size fits mixed borders and smaller gardens where full-size smokebush cultivars would quickly outgrow the space.

directions: Winecraft Black is a patented Proven Winners ColorChoice selection bred for a distinctly smaller, denser habit than older purple smokebush cultivars like Royal Purple, reaching only about 4 to 6 feet tall and wide instead of towering to 15 feet. Its rounded leaves emerge deep burgundy and darken further through the season toward near-black, setting off the airy, smoke-like plumes of small summer flowers that give the plant its common name. It is highly drought-tolerant once established and performs best in lean, well-drained soil in full sun, where the dark foliage color develops most intensely. Because it stays compact naturally, Winecraft Black needs little to no pruning to keep its shape, though it can be cut back hard in late winter if a fuller, denser mound is wanted at the cost of that year's flower plumes.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Nordine was selected at Illinois's Morton Arboretum for its superior cold hardiness among purple-leaf smokebush selections.

directions: Nordine is a bronze-red-leaved smokebush cultivar selected for holding its purplish-red foliage color further into summer than many other dark-leaf selections before shifting to yellow-orange in fall, and it is regarded as the hardiest of the purple-leaf smokebush cultivars, tolerating colder winters than Royal Purple or Velvet Cloak. It grows considerably larger than compact modern cultivars, reaching small-tree proportions with age, and produces the same airy, smoke-like plumes of small summer flowers typical of the species. Give it lean, rocky, excellently drained soil in full sun, since Nordine dislikes heavy, wet ground and performs poorly with excess fertility or moisture. Established plants are highly drought-tolerant and need only occasional structural pruning in late winter to remove crossing or damaged branches.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Variegata needs a bit more light than plain green Fatsia japonica to keep its white leaf margins crisp, but still scorches in hot direct sun.

directions: Variegata is the classic, long-cultivated variegated form of Japanese aralia, its bold, deeply lobed palmate leaves edged in creamy white rather than the solid green of the species, the mottled chartreuse blotches of 'Camouflage', or the fine speckling of 'Spider's Web'. It carries the same architectural, tropical-looking presence that makes Fatsia japonica valuable for lighting up shaded courtyards and foundation beds, with the crisp white edging adding brightness to dim corners where flowering shrubs struggle. Small, rounded clusters of white flowers appear in fall on mature plants, followed by glossy black berries that draw birds through winter. Grow it in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil sheltered from harsh wind and hot midday sun, and prune only to remove damaged or leggy stems.

common_name: Minor Yeddo Hawthorn (Dwarf Compact Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Minor's dense, naturally dwarf mound needs little pruning to stay in bounds as a low hedge or mass planting.

directions: Minor is a compact, slow-growing dwarf selection of Yeddo hawthorn, forming a dense, rounded mound of small, glossy, dark green leaves that emerge coppery-bronze before maturing, a finer texture than standard Indian hawthorn. Clusters of fragrant white flowers cover the plant in spring, sometimes followed by small dark blue-black berries that attract birds. Its low, tidy habit suits foundation plantings, low borders, and mass groundcover use where the larger species or upright cultivars like Majestic Beauty would quickly overgrow the space. Like other Rhaphiolepis, Minor is exceptionally tolerant of heat, drought, and salt spray once established, making it a dependable low-maintenance choice for coastal and Gulf Coast landscapes; space plants for good air circulation to minimize leaf spot in humid conditions.
